textContent.text: "We're here!" Audrey shouts.
Woody jumps out of the car.
"Whoa, slow down," Audrey says. She hooks Woody's leash on, and they head into the pet shop.
"Look at all the toys!" says Audrey.
Woody sees a toy shaped like a bone. He holds out his paw.
"It looks like you're pointing!" Audrey says. "You found one you like, huh, boy?"
She reaches for the toy, but Woody gets there first. He grabs it and zooms away. He knocks over some dog food, and it pours onto the floor.
"Woody! Come, now!" Audrey shouts.
Woody slowly crawls over and drops the toy.
"You're lucky you're cute," Audrey tells him.

textContent.text: "Why is there a huge crowd in town square?" Troy wondered.
Joy shook her head. "I don't know. Let's make our way over there," she said.
When they got close, Joy pointed ahead. "Look, it's a clown!" she said.
They saw the clown pull out a balloon and blow. She twisted the long balloon into a crown. Then the clown looked around the crowd and placed it on Joy's head.
"Can you make me something cool, too?" Troy asked. The clown frowned. She was out of balloons.
Then, the clown reached into her coat and pulled out a kazoo. She handed it to Troy.
"You're the best clown in town!" Troy shouted.

textContent.text: "Our friends are coming soon!" says Raccoon.
"I'll boil water for oatmeal and heat oil to cook sausage," says Bear.
Raccoon looks at the clock. "That will take too long," he says. "Let's make smoothies instead."
Bear nods. He puts the fruit in the blender and turns it on.
SPLAT! The smoothie sprays all over! Bear frowns. "Oh no! That was my fault," he cries.
Ding dong! Raccoon opens the door. "Hello, Bird and Bat," says Raccoon. "Sorry about the mess."
Bird looks inside. "Well, we enjoy cleaning," he caws. Bird and Bat fly around, scooping up the smoothie with spoons.
Bear smiles. "It's nice to have friends with wings!" he jokes.

textContent.text: Shaun sat in art class, looking at drawings around the room.
He frowned. "Flowers? Clouds? I don't want to draw those things," he said.
His teacher leaned down. "In my class, you can draw anything you like," she said.
Shaun looked around. He paused when he spotted his book in his bag. "All About Moose." "Hmmm," he thought.
He found his colored pencils. "I will make a brown body and a round head," he said.
Soon, Shaun was done. It was time to show his drawing. "This is my moose," he said, pointing to his paper. "He's cold, so I gave him a wool sweater and boots."
The class clapped. Shaun stood tall, feeling proud.

textContent.text: One night, Owen the Owl was flying around the moonlit sky. SPLASH! "What was that sound?" Owen wondered aloud.
He quickly flew down below the clouds. From the river, he heard a loud cry.
"Help!" shouted a small mouse. Owen spotted the mouse splashing in the water.
"Oh no!" he cried. "That little mouse can't get out!"
Quickly, Owen swooped down. He grabbed a piece of wood from the ground. He put it in the water. "Climb on!" Owen shouted. He pulled the mouse on the wood back to land.
"You look so cold!" Owen hooted. He wrapped his brown feathers around the little mouse.
"Thank you, Mr. Owl," the little mouse said.

textContent.text: "Moo!" shouted Claude the Cow.
Heather the Hawk flew down to the wooden fence. "What's wrong?" she asked.
"My hoof hurts," said Claude.
"Oh no! You need to rest," said Heather. "But the market still needs flowers. I'll find some help."
She flew around and found Brooke the Rabbit hopping near the trees.
"Claude can't pick flowers today," Heather said. "Want to help me gather some?"
"I'd love to!" said Brooke.
Heather flew above the meadow, spotting flowers. Brooke leapt below, picking them from the soil.
Later, Claude felt better. He went out to count the pile. "There are too few," he told Brooke.
Brooke smiled. "That's my fault," she said. "I had to eat a few. Flowers taste so good!"
